Perfect agreement on category decoding and tradeoff analysis (C43-C48). Perfect agreement on RNN modeling results (C49-C57). Agreement on RNN-fMRI correspondence limitations (C92-C96), but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing honest acknowledgment of limitations as strengthening conclusions. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the correspondence 'could be a little more comprehensive' and introducing some uncertainty about computational interpretation.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C3-C7, C97-C100). Agreement on sPCS findings (C29-C32), with OpenEval covering broader claim set including IPS and EVC. Both strongly support the frontal cortex pattern showing stronger decoding during categorization. Peer reviewers explicitly call this an 'important finding' that is 'compelling,' aligning with OpenEval's detailed statistical documentation.

Agreement on IPS findings (C28), with OpenEval covering broader ROI analysis (C25-C32). Both accept the IPS pattern as part of the distributed network results. Peer reviewers treat it as an intermediate finding in the cortical hierarchy, consistent with OpenEval's documentation of differential patterns across ROIs.

Agreement on sPCS specificity analysis (C76). Both evaluations support the control analyses comparing sPCS to other frontal ROIs. OpenEval documents this as part of broader sPCS findings (C68-C77), while peer reviewers explicitly praise these additional ROI analyses for contextualizing and adding specificity to the main effects.

Partial overlap on sPCS summary claims (C68, C71, C74). Both evaluations support these findings as part of the main conclusions.
